t:
No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall remain available for obligation beyond the current fiscal year unless expressly so provided herein.
This Act may be cited as the “Department of Transportation Appropriation Act, 1968”.

fable.w: This section only limits the availability of appropriated funds to the current fiscal year and gives the Act its short title. There is no tempting reading here: no party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, appointed to an advisory body, or given a right to sue, and no rulemaking is authorized.
fable.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall remain available for obligation beyond the current fiscal year unless expressly so provided herein.

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard appropriations clause limiting the availability of funds to the current fiscal year. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. It is purely an internal budgetary constraint.
qwen_block.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall remain available for obligation beyond the current fiscal year unless expressly so provided herein.

opus.w: This section only says that appropriations expire at the end of the fiscal year unless the Act says otherwise, and it gives the Act's short title. It does not consult outside parties, require a hearing, comment period or rulemaking, create an advisory body, or grant a right to sue. No part of the text deals with outside involvement in a federal decision, so the label is 'No' and there is no on-topic span to quote.
opus.b: The section is boilerplate in an appropriations act: one sentence on when appropriated funds lapse, and one giving the Act's short title. There is no tempting "Yes" reading here. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing or a comment period, or given a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes a fiscal rule regarding the availability of appropriated funds and provides a short title for the Act. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. There are no mentions of public comment, advisory boards, state consultation, or rights to sue.
qwen_chat.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall remain available for obligation beyond the current fiscal year unless expressly so provided herein.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because this is an appropriations act, it implicitly involves the public or states in how funds are spent. However, the text itself contains no procedural requirements for consultation, comment, or coordination with any outside party. It is purely a fiscal limitation and a citation clause.
